We’re thrilled to introduce Jessica Campbell (@soupy08), assistant coach of the @SeattleKraken, as the headlining speaker for the inaugural UNMATCHED: Gender Equity in Sports Conference – Montreal Edition, presented by @nationalbankofcanada.
 
A true hockey trailblazer, Jessica will join fellow sports pioneer @chantalmachabee on August 6 for a powerful conversation about breaking barriers and redefining what’s possible for women in sports.
 
Rooted in the theme Stronger Together, the conference will also feature inspiring voices like Portia Archer, @laurastacey7, @marinette.pichon, and many more.
 
This is more than just a moment - it’s a movement.
You don’t want to miss it!
 
//
 

Nous sommes ravis de vous présenter Jessica Campbell (@soupy08), entraîneure adjointe du @SeattleKraken, à titre d’oratrice principale de l’édition montréalaise de HORS PAIR : la conférence sur l’équité des genres dans le sport présentée par @BanqueNationale.
 
Véritable pionnière dans le monde du hockey, Jessica se joindra à une autre pionnière du sport, @chantalmachabee, le 6 août, pour une discussion percutante sur la façon de briser les barrières et de redéfinir ce qui est possible pour les femmes dans le sport.
 
Ancrée dans le thème Avancer ensemble, la conférence présentera également des voix inspirantes, telles que celles de Portia Archer, @laurastacey7, @marinette.pichon, et de bien d’autres.
 
C’est plus qu’un moment, c’est un mouvement.
Ne manquez pas cette occasion !

Thank you to the Seattle Sports Commision and the Kraken organization for the honour of Sports Story of the Year. I am humbled to be part of this proud sports city and community.

The award presented this week isn’t about me.
It’s about progress.

It’s about what happens when we stop asking if change is possible...and start proving that it is.

I may be the first woman behind an NHL bench, but I won’t be the last... because once a door opens, it doesn’t close.

Thank you to Sam Holloway, and the Seattle Kraken Ownership group. Led by the vision of David Bonderman and CEO Tod Lewieke...you didn’t just talk about change, you made it happen.

Thank you to our GM Ron Francis, for your leadership and support. You didn’t just open a door, you moved our game forward.

To our Head Coach, Dan Bylsma... this journey began 3 years ago in the AHL. Thank you for seeing me for my ability, and believing in the idea that different voices and perspectives- all knowledgeable and passionate in their own right - help build a stronger team.

This isn’t about rewriting the past...
It’s about defining the future.

And we are just getting started.

#RuthChepng’etich set the world record time at the 2024 Chicago Marathon. This achievement positioned her as the first woman to run under 2:10 in marathon history.

Originally from Oyo State in Nigeria, #RhasidatAdeleke gained traction as one of Ireland’s most celebrated sprinters. We celebrated her becoming the first Irish woman to break the 50-second barrier in the 400-meter sprint.

Kenyan-Romanian long-distance runner #JoanChelimoMelly celebrated an amazing victory in the Berlin Marathon. Melly’s achievement adds to her growing list of accolades but also inspires a new generation of runners across two continents.

The NHL welcomed its first female coach, #JessicaCampbell. Campbell brings her experience as a former player for the Canadian women’s national team to the professional league; proving that there are no limits to what women can achieve in sports.

Lastly, British mountaineer, paragliding pilot, and adventure athlete #AdrianaBrownlee cemented herself as the youngest woman to conquer all 14 of the world’s eight-thousanders this year. caption:
Part 1 of 2 // I write this not knowing where to begin...but it feels a lot like how we started this Journey 6 weeks ago lacing up the skates for the first time...Terrified, Excited, Grateful and Proud.💜

For all that need to hear this. Here we go:

Are you scared? Yes. 
Will it stop you? No. 
Why? Because it matters. 
...1 in 5 youth struggle with their mental health. That’s a lot of kids in a classroom, on a team and in a community, big or small. Exactly why we need to grab our torch, start the spark and just go for it.

We attacked the @cbcbattle with brave hearts to light up the path for others to see the way. This is our why. @asherkwacie and I were strangers 2 months ago, but promised we would combine hearts, experiences and forces for all the kids we represent. Trying best to embrace our youthful selves & show up for them. Black, White, Brown. For equality and equal playing fields. To inspire people to do more, be more. Challenging systems to allow educators to illuminate classrooms with compassion and judgement free learning. With hope that young hearts can experience how inclusive and open dialogue not only changes lives it saves them. A place where youth can express their feelings however they choose, (even if it’s in a purple hat Sofi Tukker TikTok) knowing fully, that by doing this - they’re fostering safe places.

Ultimately, we wanted kids to feel empowered to carry their own torch. To skate with us and choose to dance when life gets hard. To attempt the impossible with a fearless heart. 

To the Teachers, Coaches, Caregivers, Mentors, Health Professionals and Counsellors; and all the trusted adults who place importance on giving youth their power- you are the real heroes.

We all have a torch to carry. The story line is never perfect or may not go as hoped, but the fire is always within us to give. 

My hope is we all keep going. Sharing our light with those who need it; remembering that one decision could be the difference, one dance move, one partner, one conversation could change a life. 

One little spark can start a flame, may you never hold yours back. #youareneveralone - Team Je$her 🤜🏻💜🖤🤛🏿 @difdroyal @cbcbattle @ben_agosto @khill_co

caption: What it's meant to be #8..❤️Today's announcement with @hockeycanada marks the beginning of a new chapter and it is with a full and heavy heart that I announce my official retirement from playing the game I've cherished all of my life. I couldn't be more thankful to have been given a life that required endless sacrifice from so many people, beginning with my parents. Their love and dedication has me remembering all the early mornings at the rink, tieing up thousands of pairs of skates,  hot chocolate between periods, mini stick wars in the kitchen, driving across the board with so many tears of joy and failure along the way, I cannot thank them enough for believing in me. •I'll never forget the day #8, gave me purpose. When faced in a moment of tragedy, the game we loved became an avenue of strength through one of the most difficult times for our family. •From chasing after my big sister, following in my brother Dion and Josh's footsteps on the cold Saskatchewan rinks to moving thousands of miles from home to BC or New York...my entire journey to Team Canada has been a dream come true. •I remember looking up to my hero Cassie Campbell at the age of 5, dreaming of becoming the next “Campbell” to wear the maple leaf, and deciding to set my mind to it. Through all the hard work, endless sacrifice, sweat and tears; I’ve come to realize that no matter what path we take in hockey or life, what we set out to do, or how many medals we win, it’s most important to leave those we meet, better than we found them. • I will always remain grateful for the friendships, leadership and coaching, that made my dream a reality, pushed me to be the best that I could be and made me a better person on and off the ice. •I want to thank my teammates, the pioneers, the fans of this game, and all the inspiring individuals with Hockey Canada for making my experience with the NWT, an incredible journey. •What this game has given me will always be a part of who I am, and what I pass on to the next generation of aspiring hockey players.
